items.title: Social Security’s fate — and your benefits — are in the hands of the candidates elected this year
items.description: The program is expected to run out of money in the next six years, which is the same amount of time as a senator’s term.

items.title: The big winners of the tech wreck are biopharma stocks
items.description: The shares of large drugmakers like Lilly, Gilead and J&J keep hitting record highs.

items.title: After Intel’s historic stock drop, analysts say there’s no reason to buy the dip
items.description: “A cheaper stock does not necessarily offer better value,” one expert says.

items.title: Trump administration is illegally delaying student-debt forgiveness for tens of thousands of public servants, lawsuit alleges
items.description: Teachers, nurses and other borrowers have waited years for approval to complete their payment obligation and access debt relief, the suit claims.

items.title: My wife cried when I found out she had only $80,000 in her 401(k). I have $2.2 million. Am I wrong to be shocked?
items.description: “When I brought up retiring last spring, she said she was ready whenever I was, and I took that to mean we were in good shape.”

items.title: Private equity in your 401(k)? Heed Warren Buffett’s warning.
items.description: About 52% of people with a workplace retirement plan say they would invest in private assets if they were available in their company’s plan.

items.title: Our church has a $1.5 million bequest earning 3.75% in a savings account. Are we throwing money away?
items.description: “Given the size and long-term nature of this gift, we want to make sure the funds are managed prudently.”

items.title: In a wild October for markets, these stocks were the biggest winners and losers
items.description: Many Big Tech stocks were hit hard but the S&P 500 showed strength under the surface, with a majority of stocks showing gains for the month.

items.title: We stopped helping our neighbors with free home repairs and our friendship cooled. Who’s to blame?
items.description: “Last summer, they complained about needing to replace their roof. A few months later, they bought a new SUV.”

items.title: Data centers are a political third rail. West Virginia is grabbing it anyway.
items.description: West Virginia wants more data centers, even as other states slam the brakes on them.
